lines: Jordan Lee
+1 (555) 010-2468 | jordan.lee@example.com | example.com/code/jordan-lee
Date of birth: 14 Mar 1999 | Nationality: Canadian
EDUCATION
Western State University | M.S. in Computer Engineering | Metro City, USA | Sep 2024 - Expected Jun 2026
Eastern Institute of Technology | B.S. in Electrical Engineering | Metro City, Country | Sep 2018 - Jun 2022
EXPERIENCE
Lakeside Auto Parts | Mechanical Design Engineer | Metro City, Country | Jun 2025 - Present
- Designed stamping dies for automotive brackets in SolidWorks, cutting the scrap rate from 6% to 4% on two press lines.
- Ran tolerance stack-up analyses for 12 production parts and signed off first-article inspections with the supplier.
Mobility Systems Company | Machine Learning Engineering Intern | Metro City, USA | Oct 2024 - May 2025
- Improved diagnostic accuracy by 35% after fine-tuning a domain adapter on validated tool-use trajectories with assistant-only loss masking.
- Designed a routing layer that limits each of 3 specialist agents and an independent reviewer to their in-scope signals, cutting reviewer disagreement with specialist findings from 14% to 6%.

- Trained the triage agent with GRPO on grouped tool-use rollouts and a reward that penalises redundant calls, cutting tool calls per case 18% and end-to-end latency 5% versus the SFT baseline at equal accuracy.
- Wrote the evaluation harness the team used to compare 14 adapter checkpoints on accuracy, citation quality and latency, catching 2 accuracy regressions before release.
- Fine-tuned the adapter with assistant-only loss masking so the model would learn to reproduce the tool outputs more faithfully.

- Built a diagnostics triage branch for an industrial inspection system that screens 800+ sensor signals per case with ML-extracted features, cutting the pending-case backlog 68% in the eight weeks after launch.
Eastern Robotics Co. | Junior Software Engineer | Metro City, Country | Aug 2022 - Jul 2024
- Cut GPU memory for fine-tuning the perception models by 4x by switching from FP32 to BF16 mixed precision.
- Reduced p95 API latency from 420 ms to 180 ms by adding a request cache and batching sensor reads, with load tests that fail the build if p95 exceeds 200 ms.
- Maintained the CI pipeline for the perception team's model releases and adds automated regression checks that shortened release cycles to 3 days.
- Migrated 30 robot-fleet services from cron jobs to an event queue with retries and dead-letter handling, removing the nightly backlogs that delayed morning dispatch.
PROJECTS
Agent Runtime Suite | Owner | TypeScript, Multi-Agent Systems | Aug 2025 - Present
- Drove adoption of AI-first engineering practices across the platform, accelerating delivery and improving outcomes for downstream teams.
- Kept working context under 10K tokens across a 100-turn stress test while the raw conversation grew 100x, using budgeted context layers and staged compaction.
- Separated concurrency pools and gated cache writes on stream completion, removing nested-pool deadlocks and lost tool results under 50-way fan-out.
Research-Agent Evaluation Framework | Contributor | LLM Evaluation | Feb 2025 - Jul 2025
- Integrated 8 citation and faithfulness metrics into an open-source research-agent framework's evaluation module.
- Showed the evaluator tracks injected degradation with a Kendall correlation of 0.89 across 400+ report-level trials that removed citations, sources and claims.
- Cut the pending-case backlog by two-thirds with a triage branch that screens 800+ sensor signals per case using ML-extracted features.
SKILLS
Programming: Python, TypeScript, Git
ML & Agents: PyTorch, LoRA, GRPO, agent evaluation

items.says: The two triage bullets give different figures for the same backlog reduction.
items.because: The Mobility Systems bullet reports 68% in eight weeks, while the Research-Agent bullet reports two-thirds.

items.says: Projects should precede Experience, with Education after both.
items.because: Putting Education first makes the strongest evidence for the résumé’s agent and evaluation direction less visible.

items.says: The move from Junior Software Engineer to Machine Learning Engineering Intern needs context.
items.because: The change in titles can read as a reduction in seniority.

items.says: The move from the ML internship to mechanical design is unexplained.
items.because: Readers may not understand how the role fits the intended ML and agent direction.

items.says: The Lakeside Auto Parts entry should be shortened to one line.
items.because: It takes space that could be reduced.

items.says: The résumé includes date of birth and nationality.
items.because: These personal details do not help readers assess qualifications for the roles.

items.says: The analyses and inspections have no reported outcome.
items.because: Readers cannot tell whether they resolved an issue, verified a design or changed a decision.

items.says: The 35% diagnostic-accuracy improvement has no evaluation baseline or set.
items.because: Readers cannot tell what accuracy was assessed.

items.says: The 35% improvement does not say whether it is relative or a percentage-point change.
items.because: Readers cannot interpret the size of the improvement.

items.says: The routing constraint is difficult to parse on a scan.
The GRPO method detail precedes the results it produced.
“The team used to” is unnecessary filler.
Assistant-only loss masking does not train the model to reproduce tool outputs.
items.because: It removes tool-output tokens from the direct training loss.

items.says: The bullet repeats the masking method already described in the accuracy bullet.
items.because: It presents faithful reproduction as an intention rather than a demonstrated result.

items.says: The triage-result bullet should open the internship entry.
items.because: Its backlog reduction and system scale make it a strong lead.

items.says: “ML-extracted features” does not identify the extraction approach.
Switching from FP32 to BF16 mixed precision alone does not support a 4× GPU-memory reduction.
items.because: BF16 uses half the storage per value, and mixed-precision fine-tuning can retain other memory.

items.says: The p95 latency bullet should open the Eastern Robotics entry.
items.because: Its quantified drop lets readers see the impact first.

items.says: “Maintained” and “adds” use inconsistent tenses for an ended role.
items.because: The shift can make readers wonder whether the work is still ongoing.

items.says: The three-day release cycle has no earlier duration for comparison.
items.because: Readers cannot judge how much faster releases became.

items.says: The automated regression checks are not described specifically.
The removed nightly backlogs and delayed dispatches are not quantified.
The bullet names AI-first practices and downstream benefits without a specific practice or assessed change.
items.because: Readers cannot picture what was introduced, what improved or how the result was assessed.

items.says: The 100× raw-conversation growth lacks a comparison baseline.
items.because: The growth is hard to interpret without one.

items.says: The reliability bullet should open the Agent Runtime Suite entry.
items.because: Removing deadlocks and lost results is a concrete outcome to put first.

items.says: “Nested-pool deadlocks” and “50-way fan-out” may be unclear outside the team.
The bullet gives no before-and-after frequency for deadlocks or lost results.
items.because: Readers cannot gauge how reliably the change removed those failures.

items.says: The metric integration does not say what changed for the framework or its users.
items.because: The metric count alone does not show what the contribution enabled or why it mattered.

items.says: The evaluator finding and correlation should come before the trial details.
items.because: Leading with the result would make it easier to scan.

items.says: The evaluator-result bullet should open the Research-Agent entry.
items.because: It provides the project’s clearest evidence.

items.says: The 0.89 Kendall correlation does not identify the two variables compared.
items.because: Readers cannot tell what the result demonstrates about the evaluator.

items.says: The screening description does not show how sensor signals are used to triage cases.
items.because: The signal count shows scale, but not how the method produces the backlog reduction.

items.says: “With a triage branch that” is a wordy bridge to the screening action.
